A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEEM method and RobustVQA study. All 24 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v3, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison. Relocated and consolidated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original DEEM results on robustness, hallucination, question answering, captioning and image generation, together with controlled ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original DEEM experiments and adds perception/comprehension benchmark results, data and model scaling experiments, and a LLaVA regularization study.

M1.justification: The DEEM architecture, losses in Equations (1)-(5), three-stage training objectives and autoregressive inference remain unchanged. The new LLaVA experiment applies the existing regularizer; no revised regularization or inference procedure is specified. Expanded token and masking descriptions clarify existing components.

E1.justification: v3 adds MMVP for basic visual perception and MMBench/MMVet for visual comprehension in Tables 1-2, substantially broadening evaluation beyond v2's existing tasks. Training datasets remain unchanged. Region-captioning and image-generation evaluations are retained in Appendix C, rather than removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Emu-I, SEED, DreamLLM and SEED-X comparisons on retained benchmarks, while removing the CLIP retrieval rows and LLaVA from that comparison. LLaVA appears in a separate new controlled study. MM-Interleaved is removed from the comprehension and image-generation tables, although retained elsewhere. The original Baseline row is renamed DEEM*, not newly introduced.

E3.justification: New controlled experiments vary training-data amounts across 32K, 96K and 160K, use ConvNeXt-L and Vicuna-13B alternatives, and evaluate LLaVA with and without regularization. Table 1 also changes AVG from six to seven benchmarks, preventing direct comparison of those aggregates. The main training recipe remains unchanged between v2 Table 12 and v3 Table 11.

E4.justification: v3 Tables 4-5 add substantive tests of data/model scalability and whether diffusion feedback benefits a text-only-generation LLaVA architecture. Existing regularization, latency, resolution, coefficient, module-freezing and prompt-format analyses are retained through consolidation or relocation. The appendix qualitative examples are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Additional result rows retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive benchmark and ablation results. Table 1 changes DEEM-VQA's RobustVQA-A/R/V scores from 53.12/62.99/61.22 to 55.22/64.12/62.99, while pretrained DEEM's existing scores remain unchanged. Table 2 replaces DreamLLM's VQAv2 entry of 56.6 with 72.9 without explaining the replacement. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting gains. v3's DEEM-VQA AVG of 65.56 also conflicts with its seven listed scores, whose mean is 66.27.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, likelihood decomposition and loss formulations are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v3 introduces none. Added mechanism explanations do not constitute new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the explicit performance claim to basic visual perception, including sensitivity to orientation, quantity, color and structure. The central contributions remain diffusion feedback for image perception, RobustVQA, and an interleaved multimodal model; the conclusion is substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the applicability argument by interpreting its new studies as evidence of scalability and architecture-independent benefits extending to text-only-generation LMMs. It also attributes CLIP limitations to contrastive learning and noisy training pairs, and frames mask fine-tuning as a check for downstream harm. Appendix A retains the existing forgetting and training-overhead limitations.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly describes replacement of embeddings and the mask/image-embedding dot product. However, it drops v2's 12-block, 77-token resampler specification and Table 1's trainable-parameter counts. The detailed main training recipes, hardware, preprocessing and code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds a dedicated discussion of diffusion models for representation learning, covering classification, segmentation, matching and learned representations, and positions DEEM against that literature. It also adds SEED/SEED-X and new evaluation references, while removing the GPT4ROI discussion and citation. This substantially broadens the previous focus on multimodal generation models.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: related work moves after the experiments, its previous subsections are consolidated, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around visual perception. Region-captioning, generation and prompt-format discussions move to appendices, while ablation sections are merged. The abstract and introduction are also revised.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with additional perceptual questions and two performance panels; Figure 2 gains a token legend and expanded caption. Benchmark tables gain columns and revised row structures. v2 Tables 6-8 become v3 Table 3, and Tables 9-10 become Table 8. Other tables move to appendices, alongside substantial typography and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added perception benchmarks and scaling/LLaVA controls strengthen evidence for the method's breadth beyond v2's principal configuration, while the new representation-learning discussion improves research positioning. These gains are tempered by removing MM-Interleaved from two downstream comparisons, losing implementation details, and introducing the Table 1 aggregate inconsistency. The net quality improvement is therefore limited.
